jobs.title: Founding Account Executive, Los Angeles
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the Role

We’re seeking a Los Angeles sales professional with a track record of success in achieving new business and growing a current book of business. The ideal candidate will be driven, organized, and display a natural ability to build rapport and trust. We’re looking for that perfect blend of sales drive coupled with a customer-first mentality that will help us create loyal, happy customers.

Rho has built a substantial community in the New York startup market. Hosting community-driven events, curated get-togethers, and more for founders and teams in the ecosystem has spread the Rho brand across many verticals. Los Angeles will be growing at the same speed and the Rho team with it. You will be responsible for organizing and attending Rho-sponsored events throughout the market geared towards building community and onboarding new business.

Responsibilities

  • Event-Driven Role – Attend multiple in-person networking events every week to build relationships and engage with the startup community. Must be comfortable with frequent face-to-face interactions.

  • Identify and target high-growth startups in the Los Angeles area for Rho’s cash management platform.

  • Win new business in competitive sales against the industry’s incumbents and newer players.

  • Attend Rho-sponsored events in person to build relationships and community.

  • Develop and execute sales strategies to meet and exceed revenue targets.

  • Ramp relationships and expand referral volume through networking.

  • Advocate for client needs to inform Rho’s roadmap.

  • Win new business in competitive sales against the industry’s incumbents and newer players.

  • Construct, forecast, and manage your sales pipeline to meet company goals.

  • Deliver comprehensive product demos and answer technical inquiries.

  • Coordinate closely with customer success and implementation teams to maintain the highest level of service and experience.

Qualifications

  • 3+ years of professional experience in a closing sales role.

  • 1+ years of experience managing a book of business and carrying a quota, focusing on net-new acquisitions.

  • Previous experience working in any one of the following areas is preferred:

    • Experience selling subscription-based software technologies (SaaS), other software products, and/or financial services products.

    • Experience working with startups.

  • Top-performer with a track record of consistently exceeding quota.

  • A consummate team player who enjoys wearing multiple hats and inspiring everyone around you to do great work.

  • A builder who is excited to help shape the foundation for Rhos’ Startup Banking team in Los Angeles.

Nice-to-Have

  • Familiarity with the startup ecosystem and venture accelerators

Our people are our most valuable asset. The budgeted base salary for this role is $83,000 - $115,000 with an OTE of $126,000 - $220,000 Base salary may vary depending on relevant experience, skills, and business needs. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, healthcare benefits and paid time off.

Diversity is a core value at Rho. We’re passionate about building and sustaining an inclusive and equitable environment for all those involved with our mission, including employees, contractors, candidates, customers and vendors. We believe every member of the Rho community enriches our ability to provide a broad range of ways to understand and engage with the market, identify problems, and drive solutions that align with our mission. We welcome all qualified applications and support each of our Rho’ers with ongoing professional growth opportunities.

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the Role

As a Senior Product Designer at Rho, you will champion the craft of design to deliver experiences that are not only functional but thoughtfully refined. You’ll take end-to-end ownership of complex product areas, consistently holding a high bar for usability, visual polish, and quality of execution. With an instinct for user behavior and a relentless attention to detail, you'll bring clarity to ambiguous problems and advocate for the end user in every decision. Working closely with product and engineering partners, you'll lead the creation of intuitive solutions that feel seamless, scalable, and rooted in empathy—ensuring every design moment reflects Rho's commitment to frictionless finance.

Responsibilities

  • Lead design efforts for end-to-end product features across multiple surfaces

  • Own complex design problems with minimal oversight—from exploration to polished execution.

  • Collaborate deeply with product managers and engineers to shape scope, identify dependencies, and optimize user flows.

  • Define interaction patterns and craft scalable, accessible solutions informed by data and user research.

  • Develop prototypes to test concepts, gather feedback, and drive alignment.

  • Uphold and evolve design quality by considering both micro-interactions and holistic experience.

  • Communicate ideas clearly across design critiques, cross-functional meetings, and stakeholder reviews.

  • Contribute to design system enhancements and advocate for design quality across teams.

Qualifications

  • 4+ years of experience designing digital products, with a portfolio demonstrating end-to-end ownership. Fintech experience preferred but is not necessary

  • Skilled in prototyping, UI/UX, interaction design, and visual polish.

  • Proven ability to work autonomously, plan work, and push projects forward independently.

  • Comfortable designing for ambiguity, resolving complex workflows, and simplifying edge cases.

  • Strong collaboration and communication skills; experience presenting to executives and external partners.

  • Familiar with applying qualitative and quantitative research methods to inform decisions.

  • Experience working with or contributing to a design system.

  • Adaptable, pragmatic, and empathetic—able to thrive in fast-changing, collaborative environments

Our people are our most valuable asset. The salary range for this role is $160,000 - $220,000. Base salary may vary depending on relevant experience, skills, and business needs. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, healthcare benefits, and paid time off.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the Role

We're looking for an expert Account Manager to manage a portfolio of our largest B2B relationships. You will work with your peers on the Customer Success team and your Manager to develop and execute repeatable tactics for onboarding and managing ongoing relationships with the businesses in your portfolio. Your north star is to drive Rho product adoption for your clients at scale, allowing you to grow your customers' revenue and maintain high retention. In this role, you will work highly collaboratively with your teammates on the Success team and cross-functionally with the Product and Customer Service teams.

Responsibilities

  • Manage, retain, and expand existing client relationships in our middle-market, VC-backed start ups, and commercial segments.

  • Strategically collaborate with the Account Executive Team (Sales) to efficiently and effectively hand off and onboard new clients.

  • Build and nurture relationships with key accounts to understand and address their business needs, priorities, goals, and challenges to maximize client adoption of Rho’s entire product suite and services.

  • Guide senior customer stakeholders through the changes needed to unlock Rho's full value, providing guidance to help them design the optimal enablement and adoption strategy to maximize their business value.

  • Track and report key account metrics, such as revenue growth, retention, and customer satisfaction.

  • Identify upsell opportunities and deliver consultative value.

Key attributes

  • Self-motivated with impeccable interpersonal and communication skills.

  • Bias for action, enthusiasm about technology and fintech, comfort with ambiguity, and high speed.

  • A high degree of comfort with drawing insights from analytics reports.

  • A valued team member who upholds Rho’s mission and professional values.

Qualifications

  • 2+ years of professional experience in a client-facing Customer Success/Account Management role

  • Has experience managing large-scale implementations with 50+ users

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills

  • A track record of managing a large portfolio of clients efficiently and at scale

  • Prior experience working in B2B SaaS, high-growth preferable

  • BA degree or higher

  • Prior background in accounting, finance, cards, or payment is preferred

Our people are our most valuable asset. This role is based out of our San Francisco office, with a base salary of $107,500 to $125,000 and an OTE of up to $145,000. Base salary may vary depending on relevant experience, skills, geographic location, and business needs. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, healthcare benefits and paid time off.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the Role

As a Senior Software Engineer at Rho, you'll build the financial infrastructure powering the next generation of founders. This isn't a role where you sit inside a lane. You'll move across the stack, own problems end-to-end, and talk directly to the customers using what you ship. We're hiring engineers who are restless about impact, reach for AI tools the way other people reach for documentation, and genuinely want to understand why what they're building matters.

What You'll Do

  • Own problems from scoping to production. Write the code, ship it, watch it land.

  • Work across the stack. You go where the problem is, not where your comfort zone ends.

  • Talk to customers. Sit in on calls, read support tickets, watch session replays. Build what people actually need.

  • Use AI in your daily workflow. Code generation, debugging, spec drafting, and spot where it changes what's possible.

  • Move fast and iterate in the open. Get something in front of users, then make it better.

  • Pick up what's falling. If something's broken, fix it.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

  • Genuine full-stack flexibility. You've shipped across the stack and don't treat the backend/frontend divide as a hard boundary.

  • Genuine AI fluency. You use these tools every day and think about where they raise the ceiling on what you can build.

  • A bias to ship. You'd rather get something in front of a user than perfect it in a doc.

  • Customer curiosity. You want to know the person on the other side of what you're building, and you'll go find out.

  • High agency. You make progress when things are unclear, surface problems early, and own your outcomes.

Compensation & Benefits

Our people are our most valuable asset. The salary range for this role is $170,000 - $270,000. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, healthcare benefits and paid time off.

A role for those committed to designing with uncommon care.

About the Role

We're looking for a Founding Banking GTM to research, identify, and acquire new clients through self-generated leads and establishing active partnerships on a local and national level. You will work with Rho leaders and team members across the organization to deliver on our mission of making finance frictionless for organizations by promoting and implementing Rho’s differentiated technology to mid-market clients.

Responsibilities

  • Generate new business opportunities by identifying and prospecting potential middle-market businesses.

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with existing and prospective clients to maximize account retention and identify upselling or cross-selling opportunities.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the Role

Rho is hiring an IT Engineer to own the technology backbone that keeps our SF office and distributed team running. You'll be the go-to person for employee IT support, device and identity management, and the systems and tooling that help Rho move fast. This is a hands-on, in-office role based in our SF office — ideal for someone who loves solving problems for their colleagues and building scalable IT operations at a high-growth fintech.

 

Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for all employee IT support — hardware, software, access, and troubleshooting — with a focus on fast, friendly resolution.

  • Own device lifecycle management across macOS and Windows, including procurement, provisioning, MDM, and secure offboarding.

  • Administer core identity and SaaS systems (SSO, Google Workspace, Slack, and related tools), including access onboarding and offboarding.

  • Manage the NYC office's IT infrastructure — networking, AV, conference rooms, and on-site hardware.

  • Build and document IT processes, runbooks, and self-service resources that scale as Rho grows.

  • Partner with Security, People, and Finance on access controls, compliance, and asset management.

  • Lead IT onboarding for new hires and ensure a seamless day-one experience.

 

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of IT support or IT operations experience, ideally in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

  • Hands-on expertise administering macOS and Windows, MDM tools, and identity/SSO platforms.

  • Strong working knowledge of Google Workspace, Slack, and common SaaS administration.

  • Experience managing office IT infrastructure, including networking, AV, and conference room technology.

  • Excellent troubleshooting skills and a customer-service mindset — you make IT feel easy for your colleagues.

  • A clear communicator who can document processes and support non-technical teammates.

  • Willing and able to work on-site 5 days per week in our SF office.

 

Our people are our most valuable asset. The salary range for this role is $90,000 - $180,000. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, healthcare benefits and paid time off.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the Role

At Rho, we seek to attract, develop and retain extraordinarily talented people. We believe that who we hire is central to what we can accomplish. As our Talent Partner, your job will be to uphold that exceptional standard and refine the infrastructure that enables us to hire great people.

You will own your funnels end-to-end, improve our Talent operating rhythm, and leverage AI as a force-multiplier. Our People function has already made significant inroads embedding AI into their workflows and we empower every member of the team to be a builder.

This role reports directly to Rho’s VP of People & Talent and is based out Rho's NYC, SF, or SLC office, 5 days a week.

What You’ll Do

Build relationships with the best talent in the tech ecosystem and find creative ways to connect with people.

Focus on quality over quantity. We know that a lean team of A+ talent is infinitely better than a large team of B-players.

Strengthen our talent brand: Partner with marketing to run events, brainstorm

Develop rigorous hiring processes across the business and advise hiring teams on building better searches.

Treat recruiting like half art, half science: Find creative ways to position Rho before the strongest operators in the business; A/B test messaging; take a human-first approach.

Obsess over our metrics and beating them, all the time.

Go where you are needed. Everyone at Rho goes beyond their job description - whether it's hiring for a G&A role or guiding someone to their interview room, this role is no exception.

What You Bring

  • 5 or more years of full-cycle recruiting experience

  • A passion for experimentation and craft: you multiply your leverage with AI, try new tools, and refuse to stop until you get it right.

  • Experience operating in high-accountability environments (startups, fintech, financial services, or similarly rigorous orgs).

  • High ownership and accountability—you take responsibility for getting the job done.

  • Strong knowledge of the talent market—where to find excellent builders, and how to speak their language.

  • Operational excellence—you know how to run a disciplined search and coach hiring managers along the way.

  • Clear, persuasive communication and storytelling skills.

  • A bias toward action and sense of ownership.

  • NYC: $120,000 - $220,000

  • Salt Lake City: $90,000 - $156,000

Rho is seeking a client-focused, entrepreneurial Financial Advisor / Registered Representative to help deliver modern wealth management solutions to founders, executives, business owners, and high-growth companies. This role combines fiduciary financial advice with the speed and innovation of a fintech platform.

The ideal candidate is a licensed investment adviser representative (Series 65) who understands both traditional wealth management and the evolving fintech ecosystem. You are comfortable working in a technology-driven environment, building trusted client relationships, and collaborating across product, operations, and engineering teams to create an exceptional client experience.

  • Serve as a fiduciary advisor to individuals, founders, executives, and business owners.

  • Educate clients on digital wealth management tools and fintech capabilities.

  • Maintain accurate client records and ensure compliance with SEC, RIA, and internal policies.

You will handle inquiries ranging from basic technical issues, such as password resets, to complex service questions, such as guidance on ERP integrations or setting up an expense management policy on the platform. This role is based full-time in our Salt Lake City office and offers the opportunity to build strong customer service and finance operations skills at a growing company.

  • Customer issue resolution: Address and resolve client issues via chat, phone, email, and text, applying good judgment and Rho's service standards in every interaction.

  • Service documentation: Document common client issues and resolutions to help build the team's knowledge base.

  • Feedback collection: Gather client feedback to help identify service improvements.

  • Team communication: Document and communicate ongoing issues to teammates and leadership for follow-up when needed.

  • Process adherence: Follow established protocols and procedures for client service delivery.

  • A passion for talent and a deep belief in the value of a great candidate experience.

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

The Role

Rho is hiring Product Managers, but what we truly seek are GMs/Product CEOs. You'll own a meaningful surface of the platform end-to-end — close enough to the work and close enough to the customer that your judgment is earned, not inherited from a roadmap. You'll know what founders need before they ask, because you've built the intuition that comes from proximity, not process.

How products get built is fundamentally changing. AI is collapsing the line between thinking about something and making it real. The best PMs right now aren't just writing specs — they're prototyping with frontier models, testing ideas the same afternoon they have them, and building product that couldn't have existed a year ago. If that's already how you work, keep reading.

Rho is rebuilding the finance stack for the innovation economy. What happens next depends on the quality of our decisions and the speed at which we make them. The PMs we hire are how we get there.

What You'll Do

Operate like a founder. Your surface is your company: its metrics are your P&L, its problems are yours whether or not they're in your job description. Nobody assigns founders their work. Default to motion — ship the scrappy version, learn, ship again, and unblock yourself instead of waiting. The surfaces you touch move faster because you're on them.

And build for them. Develop a deep, almost unfair understanding of how early-stage companies think about money, time, and risk. Design for the workflow they don't know they want yet — the desire path, not the paved one.

Own a problem space, not a problem. Not a feature, not a ticket queue — a living territory of customer problems that shift and collide. Frame the ones that matter, sharpen the hypothesis, define success before you build, and see it through to landing in a founder's hands. The map will change under you; redraw it and keep moving.

Decide what matters most — and re-decide when the facts change. Make deliberate calls about what to do now, next, and never. Hold them loosely: when the evidence says pivot, you pivot without ego. A PM who can't say no is just a project manager with better slides.

Work at the frontier. AI is your leverage in both directions: it 10x's how you work — more ideas tested, more prototypes built, more customer insight absorbed, more shipped — and it expands what you can build, product experiences that weren't possible twelve months ago. You're expected to find both. When a new capability drops, you're the one asking what it unlocks for our customers.

Get in the weeds. You're prototyping, pressure-testing, and iterating alongside design and engineering — with opinions about the details. Bring people along while you're there: partner deeply across Engineering, Design, Operations, GTM, and leadership, and communicate the why so well the team could make your calls without you in the room.

Who You Are

  • You have 3+ years building products — as a founder, PM, or engineer or equivalent experience in a fast-paced, high-growth environment — and you've shipped work you're proud to put your name on.

  • You have frontier fluency. You work with AI daily — prototyping, analyzing, drafting, automating — and you can point to something you shipped or changed because a new capability made it possible. Not theorizing; doing.

  • You have taste. You hold your own view of what good looks like, obsess over the details, and know that in a banking product, every interaction carries trust.

  • You have discovery rigor. You can articulate the problem, the hypothesis, and how you'll know it worked before you've written a spec.

  • You build. You're not above opening a prototype, sketching a flow, or pulling the data yourself.

  • You think like a founder. You've been one, worked next to one, or operated like one — you take ownership past the edges of your role, and you pull things over the line that would die in someone else's backlog.

  • You're at home in ambiguity. You make calls on incomplete information and treat a pivot as new information, not a setback. Plans change; you're the steady one when they do.

  • You bring people with you. You build trust quickly, communicate proactively, and can align a room even when the answer is no.

  • You crave a team that pushes you — smart, ambitious people who make the work fun and help you grow faster than you thought possible.

Our people are our most valuable asset. Our target compensation range for this role is $165,000 - $320,000. Compensation will be determined by leveling and performance throughout the interview process. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, comprehensive healthcare benefits, and paid time off.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the Role

Rho is seeking an Associate Compliance Officer to support our onboarding compliance team. You'll own day-to-day customer due diligence (CDD) and Know Your Business (KYB) work for new client onboarding — gathering and verifying documentation, running risk assessments against established frameworks, and escalating issues to senior compliance staff. You'll play a vital part in keeping Rho compliant with BSA/AML, OFAC, and FinCEN requirements while maintaining the application review velocity our customers expect. This full-time, onsite role is a strong fit for someone looking to build a career in banking or fintech compliance within a growing, mission-driven company.

What You'll Do

  • Support the CDD and KYC/KYB processes for new client onboarding by gathering and organizing required documentation in accordance with BSA/AML, OFAC, and FinCEN requirements

  • Collect and verify client documentation, including business formation documents, ownership structures, and beneficial ownership information, escalating discrepancies to senior team members

  • Assist in performing risk assessments on potential clients using established frameworks and checklists

  • Flag and escalate suspicious activity or potential compliance issues identified during onboarding to senior compliance staff

  • Coordinate with internal teams, including sales and operations, to collect outstanding client information and ensure timely onboarding

  • Maintain accurate and complete records of client onboarding files, compliance decisions, and supporting documentation in accordance with team standards

  • Support periodic reviews of existing client accounts by gathering and organizing documentation for senior team review

  • Assist in the preparation of compliance reports and data pulls as directed by management

  • Support updates to policies and procedures by documenting process changes and maintaining version-controlled records

  • Utilize compliance technology platforms to process onboarding tasks, input data, and maintain system accuracy

  • Follow established onboarding compliance policies and procedures, providing feedback to senior staff on potential process improvements

  • Participate in compliance training sessions and apply best practices to daily onboarding tasks, developing foundational knowledge of fintech and banking regulation through ongoing training and self-study

  • Take on other activities as determined by your supervisor

You Have

  • A Bachelor's degree in finance, business, or a related field preferred

  • 1–2 years of experience in compliance, finance, banking, or a related operations role

  • Working understanding of BSA/AML, OFAC, and FinCEN requirements, including CDD and KYB concepts

  • Exceptional attention to detail, strong organization, and a proactive approach to problem-solving

  • Ability to manage a queue independently, prioritize across competing deadlines, and meet required service levels

  • Comfort working in compliance technology platforms and learning new systems quickly

  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the judgment to know when to escalate

Compensation & Schedule

  • Full-time, salaried position with benefits

  • Onsite work environment

  • Standard weekday schedule; occasional flexibility may be needed to meet onboarding volume

  • Opportunity for growth into senior compliance roles based on performance and business needs

jobs.title: Staff / Principal Product Designer, Design Systems
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

Rho — New York (in person)

Rho is building the best business banking platform on earth. Not "one of." The best.

We're looking for a Staff or Principal Product Designer to own our design system, the governed, in code foundation that everything we ship stands on. This is not a role where you maintain a Figma library and file tickets. This is the role where you define the frontend layer of a financial operating system that companies trust with their money.

It's a long post on purpose. We'd rather you know exactly what this is before you apply.

What you'd actually own

Our design system is becoming the governed frontend layer of the product, components in code, rules enforced through lint and CI, documentation an AI agent can query and build against on spec. You would own that. The architecture, the tokens, the primitives, the motion language, the governance, the contribution model, and the standards that let 80 plus engineers and PMs ship on bar without a designer babysitting every pixel.

You'll partner with our frontend guild, our engineers, and the design team as genuine equals, not as a service desk. You'll decide what a component is, how it behaves, how it moves, what it enables, and where it must not bend. You'll set the craft bar for the entire org and then build the system that makes hitting that bar the path of least resistance.

Who this is for

You've been doing this for a while. We mean it, at least 7 years of product design experience, with real design systems ownership at scale. Not "contributed to a design system." Owned one. Built one. Governed one. Watched it get abused and fixed the governance so it couldn't happen again.

You are the kind of person who:

  • Designs in code, or is hungry to. You believe Figma is not the build environment, and that designing in the real medium eliminates a whole category of hidden QA cost. If the phrase "design engineer" makes you lean forward, hi.

  • Has genuine taste and a serious bar for it. Branding, typography, motion, microinteractions: you sweat all of it. You have opinions about easing curves and you can defend them. A transition that feels half a beat off bothers you until it's fixed.

  • Owns your craft, doesn't inherit it. You can point at a visual language and say "I built that," not "that was set before I got there and I adjusted the fonts."

  • Builds systems, not screens. You think in primitives, states, edge cases, and two-way doors. When something breaks at a thousand users, you already designed for it.

  • Ships, then sharpens. You move fast, you work out loud, you share the messy middle instead of disappearing for three weeks and returning with a monument. Perfect but late is a fail here.

  • Has low ego and high standards at the same time. You hold a firm craft bar and you genuinely want the critique. You defend decisions with reasoning, not with "it's my stylistic choice."

  • Gets the domain, or is dying to. Financial workflows are dense, multi-role, permission scoped, and unforgiving. You find that fun, not frightening.

Who this is NOT for

A few honest filters, to save us both time.

Do not apply to this role if you are junior. This is a Staff/Principal position. If you're earlier in your career, we'd genuinely love to meet you, we just want you in the right process. Apply for our product designer role instead: https://www.rho.co/careers/f4ece49b-3b53-4ffb-861f-9cc972c10b27

It's also probably not your fit if:

  • Your portfolio is process decks, tiny mockups, and journey maps, and the actual UI is nowhere to be found. We evaluate craft at the pixel level. If we can't see it, we can't hire it.

  • Your idea of a design system is a color palette and a component library nobody governs.

  • Motion and micro interactions are afterthoughts to you rather than part of the craft.

  • You need a fully specced ticket before you can move, and ambiguity makes you freeze.

  • You want to be handed the vision. We want someone who brings one.

  • "Move fast" reads to you as "lower the quality bar." Here it means the opposite, the bar is high AND the pace is high, and the system you build is how those two coexist.

  • You lead with an AI chatbot case study. We love AI and use it every day. But a conversational UI is not a demonstration of end-to-end product craft.

How we work

Small pods. Artifact first. Designers own their surfaces end to end, including research, QA, and the fight to get it shipped right. We use AI natively and expect you to. The design team is heads down on building the governed frontend layer this quarter, and this role is central to it.

We're in the office in New York because the best systems work happens shoulder to shoulder, obsessing over a real screen.

The bar

Restraint over decoration. Confidence over noise. Interfaces that feel calm because someone sweated every detail so the user never has to, and that feel alive because the motion is considered, not bolted on. We care about how money moving feels, how a card creation confirms, how a state transition lands. If "it looks fun, but does it do anything" is a question you ask yourself unprompted, you'll fit right in.

How to apply

If you've read this far and you're already thinking about how you'd architect our token layer, we should talk.

Come ready to do two things when we meet, walk us through a real, working file (not just the polished case study frames), and show us a design system you actually built and governed. Bring one deeply complex, systems level project and one piece you're proud of at the pixel level, and tell us plainly which decisions were yours.

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist/ML
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the Role

Our team is looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join our data products team. This role has significant latitude to shape how modeling, evaluation, and ML infrastructure work here: the standards, tooling, and processes you help establish will influence how models get built for a long time to come.

This is intentionally a hybrid role. At many companies, data science and ML infrastructure are split into separate functions: data scientists author and train models, while a dedicated platform team owns deployment, observability, and retraining. At Rho, we need someone who can do both, someone who can build the model and reason clearly about how it gets deployed, monitored, and retrained in production. You'll work on high-leverage problems like our transaction coding suggestion engine, OCR/document understanding pipeline, and RAG-based and agentic systems, while also helping build the underlying foundation: evaluation frameworks, model deployment and monitoring practices, and the infrastructure decisions that determine whether ML at Rho is reliable and scalable. This role requires genuine fluency in ML infrastructure and evals, not just modeling - you should be as comfortable discussing feature store design or eval harness architecture with data engineers as you are validating a model's statistical soundness.

Technologies we use for data: Python, Snowflake, DBT, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes, MLflow, Terraform, Prometheus, Google Cloud Services, Omni, Hex, PowerBI

Responsibilities:

  • Help define and evolve Rho's ML/DS practices: how models get evaluated, deployed, monitored, versioned, and retrained

  • Design and implement evaluation frameworks and eval harnesses that give the company real confidence in model quality, before and after launch

  • Build and own high-impact models and analyses powering products like transaction coding suggestions, OCR/document understanding, and RAG/agentic systems

  • Make and document key ML infrastructure decisions (model registries, feature stores, serving patterns, monitoring/alerting for drift and degradation) in close partnership with data engineering

  • Set technical standards and best practices that help the ML/DS practice scale as the team grows

  • Translate ambiguous business problems into well-scoped modeling questions

  • Design and analyze experiments (A/B tests, causal inference) to validate model impact rigorously

  • Advocate for and drive adoption of ML infrastructure and tooling improvements as needs grow

Requirements:

  • 6+ years of experience in data science, applied ML, or a related quantitative field, with a track record of shipping models into production

  • Deep, hands-on understanding of ML infrastructure: model registries, feature stores, serving architectures, monitoring/observability for models, and retraining pipelines

  • Strong experience designing evaluation frameworks and evals for ML systems;, including offline metrics and ongoing production evaluation

  • Comfortable operating as a hybrid DS/infrastructure practitioner:, someone who doesn't hand a model off to a platform team and walk away, but who can own it end to end when needed

  • Experience helping establish or mature ML practices, standards, or infrastructure within a team and company

  • Strong programming skills in Python, with solid SQL

  • Comfortable making infrastructure trade-off decisions jointly with data/platform engineers, and able to speak credibly on both the modeling and systems sides

  • Experience with statistical modeling, machine learning techniques, and experiment design

  • Excellent communication skills; able to influence technical direction and bring both technical and non-technical stakeholders along

Nice To Haves:

  • Experience with RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) systems, vector databases, or building/deploying agents

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the Role

Rho is hiring a Workplace Generalist in New York to own a world-class experience for everyone who walks through our doors. As an in-office company, we take our spaces seriously. Our workplaces are environments that foster connection, collaboration, and higher-quality work — and this role is how critical to making that a reality every day.

What You'll Do

  • Partner with People E&E on space planning, sublease transitions, and new-market buildouts. Localize Rho’s workplace standard for NYC; stay on the real estate roadmap.

  • Be NYC’s point of contact for workplace and space. Build trust across every department. Close gaps before they become tickets.

  • Share what you learn here as Rho stands up new offices. Your fingerprints should show up in the next city.

  • Own NYC's workplace programming calendar end-to-end — events, activations, community moments. Concept through execution. Logistics and budget.

  • Walk the office and monitor supplies, equipment, cleanliness.

  • Prioritize every day. Triage incoming work, protect the team from noise, and set the order of operations.

  • Support administrative tasks for the People function including mailing, I9 verification, and more.

  • Build the system behind the work — tracking, docs, handoffs — so workplace is visible and doesn’t live in one person’s head.

  • Own the vendor roster across cleaning, maintenance, catering, and security. Source and manage vendor ops.

  • Manage inventory and procurement so our offices stay fully stocked.

  • Own the first-day and last-day experience in NYC, including access provisioning.

  • Treat AI as a force multiplier. Use it every day on writing, research, planning, and ops — then spend the time you save on taste and judgment.

  • Track what’s working (budget-to-actual, vendor performance, programming quality) and use it to raise the standard — and to change how the work gets done.

About You

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.

  • 1–3 years in events, hospitality, workplace, or operations.

  • Sharp taste. You notice what’s off in a room and you can’t leave it unsolved.

  • You’re willing to do the unglamorous work — and impatient enough to build it into something better.

  • Discretion and professionalism. You’ll be in rooms with visitors, executives, and sensitive work.

  • Strong time management, precision, and a bias toward saying the thing early.

  • You build systems. Comfortable in Jira, Slack, and Notion — and quick to adopt better tooling when the work demands it.

  • Able to lift and move boxes.

  • You already use AI to get more done. You default to it as leverage, not a novelty.

  • Vendor management, negotiation, or budget oversight is a plus.

  • Conversational Spanish is a plus.

Our people are our most valuable asset. The salary range for this role is $70,000 - $90,000. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, healthcare benefits and paid time off.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

Financial Crime Analyst

We're looking for an experienced financial crime analyst to support our overall fraud and anti-money laundering (AML) strategy and operations, working alongside and supporting the Financial Crime lead as a critical member of the team. As a core member of the team, you will have a unique opportunity to learn and apply your previous experience, design and innovate financial crime detection systems, while conducting data analysis and being actively engaged cross-functionally. You will help lead efforts to build a best-in-class program that directly supports a seamless and frictionless client experience while reducing fraud and AML risk exposure and protecting against financial loss and regulatory risk.

Responsibilities:

  • Analyze fraud and AML alerts and cases to identify, investigate, and prevent fraudulent activity and suspicious transactions

  • Conduct transaction monitoring reviews and assess activity against AML/BSA typologies, escalating as needed

  • Prepare and file Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) and maintain supporting documentation in line with regulatory requirements

  • Assist customers by preparing and responding to inquiries related to fraud and financial crime investigations, and support the resolution of incidents

  • Document investigation processes and outcomes to maintain audit-ready records

  • Maintain department productivity goals and quality standards

  • Collaborate with the Financial Crime team to support and refine our operations, working cross-functionally with Client Services, Financial Operations, Compliance, and Transaction Monitoring teams

  • Maintain regular communication with team members to ensure maximum efficiency in recovery efforts and support ongoing strategy management

  • Deep dive into individual fraud and AML event vectors to perform root cause analyses

  • Support KYC/CIP and customer due diligence (CDD/EDD) reviews as needed

Qualifications:

  • 2+ years of experience in fraud risk, AML/BSA, and/or payments operations in banking and/or financial services

  • Experience using systems such as Excel, Google Workspace, Looker, and Slack

  • Understanding of how to leverage AI to improve investigation efficiency and drive improvements in alert query quality, tuning, and detection logic

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

  • Ability to work independently, capable of taking ownership and acting as the primary contact for fraud and financial crime-related issues when needed

  • Strong working knowledge of compliance and payment regulations, including Reg E, NACHA, AML/BSA, KYC/CIP, OFAC, FinCEN, SAR/CTR filing requirements, and related frameworks

Nice to Have:

  • Experience within Micro SMB/SMB business cards, payments, invoices, lending, or related financial industries

  • Experience in high-growth startups, specifically global fintechs and/or neobanks for corporate clients

  • Experience with U.S. fraud and AML risk for ACH, Card, Checks, and Wires with a global or large financial institution, and key understanding of common fraud and money laundering typologies

  • CAMS (Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist) certification or actively pursuing one

  • Experience with case management or monitoring systems (e.g., Actimize, Sardine, Alloy, Unit21)

Compensation:

Our people are our most valuable asset. The salary range for this role is $60,000 – $90,000 in Salt Lake City. Base salary may vary depending on relevant experience, skills, and business needs. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, healthcare benefits, and paid time off.

We’re passionate about building and sustaining an inclusive and equitable environment for all those involved with our mission, including employees, contractors, candidates, customers, and vendors. We believe every member of the Rho community enriches our ability to provide a broad range of ways to understand and engage with the market, identify problems, and drive solutions that align with our mission. We welcome all qualified applications and support each of our Rho’ers with ongoing professional growth opportunities.

In Brand, you’ll own campaign project management, keeping launches on schedule from brief to go-live. You’ll also run brand lift analysis so we can measure what each campaign actually moves.   • Run a weekly written review across all three pillars (not a dashboard nobody opens) so slipping work surfaces early instead of reaching the VP of Marketing the night before it matters.

  • Translate the outputs of Growth Engineering and the data science team (funnel performance, cost per funded account, channel health) into reporting marketing, exec, and the board actually run on. You consume these models, you don't build them.

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re hiring a Marketing Operations Manager to be the backbone of Rho’s marketing org. This person keeps our work across the team running smoothly, so we can move quickly and leadership always knows what’s live, what’s working, and where to focus next.

In Brand, you’ll own campaign project management, keeping launches on schedule from brief to go-live. You’ll also run brand lift analysis so we can measure what each campaign actually moves. In Growth, you’ll facilitate our experimentation program, from setting up tests to sharing what we learned. You’ll also manage the systems and tech stack the team depends on every day.

Across the org, you’ll build and run the system of record: one place where every workstream’s owner, status, and key metric lives. You’ll partner with Growth Engineering and the data science team to turn their work into a reporting cadence that marketing, the exec team, and the board rely on. Working closely with the VP of Marketing, you’ll have the context to spot what needs attention and the process discipline to raise it early, so the whole team stays aligned, hits its numbers, and scales.



RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the system of record: one place where every workstream across Growth, Brand, and Community is tracked against its owner, status, and the metric it's supposed to move.

 - Run a weekly written review across all three pillars (not a dashboard nobody opens) so slipping work surfaces early instead of reaching the VP of Marketing the night before it matters.

 - Translate the outputs of Growth Engineering and the data science team (funnel performance, cost per funded account, channel health) into reporting marketing, exec, and the board actually run on. You consume these models, you don't build them.

 - Track every vendor and spend commitment against sign-off status; flag anything moving forward without it before it becomes a fait accompli.

 - Maintain a single, current version of marketing strategy and planning docs, replacing the scattered state across Slack, Notion, and individual owners' heads.

 - Run the cadence on hiring, budget, and planning asks that go to Devonaire, Bojan, and other cross-functional partners, so those requests are tracked to a decision instead of going quiet.

 - Keep a live map of who owns what, including backup owners for anything with single-threaded risk, so no function or vendor relationship depends on one person.

 - Flag ownership gaps and conflicting priorities across pillars directly, rather than letting them resolve themselves by default.

 - Run the experimentation program for Growth: intake, prioritization, test design standards, sprint cadence, and a shared learnings log.

 - Facilitate a weekly or bi-weekly experiment cadence across Growth, including hypothesis writing, success criteria, and kill and scale decisions.


REQUIREMENTS

 - You've designed and run an incrementality or lift test (holdout, geo-lift, PSA-style), not just read about the concept. You know what breaks a naive test — seasonality, cross-channel halo, saturation — and how to control for it.

 - Fluent SQL, and you've built and owned dbt models in a real warehouse. This isn't a role you can do from platform UIs.

 - You've owned marketing or GTM data where the number mattered financially, and defended a CAC or attribution figure to a skeptical exec.

 - You've reconciled conflicting numbers across ad platforms, a CRM, and a warehouse, and can explain the gap rather than picking the flattering one.

 - Systems experience, not just analysis: forms, routing, CRM sync, reverse ETL, taxonomy. Comfortable owning plumbing.

 - You define metrics instead of waiting to be handed them.

 - Judgment on PII and compliance in a regulated financial services context.

 - Comfortable as the only person in your function, working across marketing, data engineering, sales ops, and growth without authority over any of them.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Fintech, banking, or another regulated environment.

 - Snowflake, dbt, Hightouch, Salesforce, HubSpot.

 - Measurement for AI search and answer engine visibility. It's an active channel for us and barely instrumented anywhere. 


Our people are our most valuable asset. The base salary for this role is $130-180K. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, healthcare benefits and paid time off.

We’re passionate about building and sustaining an inclusive and equitable environment for all those involved with our mission, including employees, contractors, candidates, customers and vendors. About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

Financial Crime Analyst

We're looking for an experienced financial crime analyst to support our overall fraud and anti-money laundering (AML) strategy and operations, working alongside and supporting the Financial Crime lead as a critical member of the team. As a core member of the team, you will have a unique opportunity to learn and apply your previous experience, design and innovate financial crime detection systems, while conducting data analysis and being actively engaged cross-functionally. You will help lead efforts to build a best-in-class program that directly supports a seamless and frictionless client experience while reducing fraud and AML risk exposure and protecting against financial loss and regulatory risk.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Analyze fraud and AML alerts and cases to identify, investigate, and prevent fraudulent activity and suspicious transactions

  • Conduct transaction monitoring reviews and assess activity against AML/BSA typologies, escalating as needed

  • Prepare and file Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) and maintain supporting documentation in line with regulatory requirements

  • Assist customers by preparing and responding to inquiries related to fraud and financial crime investigations, and support the resolution of incidents

  • Document investigation processes and outcomes to maintain audit-ready records

  • Maintain department productivity goals and quality standards

  • Collaborate with the Financial Crime team to support and refine our operations, working cross-functionally with Client Services, Financial Operations, Compliance, and Transaction Monitoring teams

  • Maintain regular communication with team members to ensure maximum efficiency in recovery efforts and support ongoing strategy management

  • Deep dive into individual fraud and AML event vectors to perform root cause analyses

  • Support KYC/CIP and customer due diligence (CDD/EDD) reviews as needed

     

Qualifications:

  • 2+ years of experience in fraud risk, AML/BSA, and/or payments operations in banking and/or financial services

  • Experience using systems such as Excel, Google Workspace, Looker, and Slack

  • Understanding of how to leverage AI to improve investigation efficiency and drive improvements in alert query quality, tuning, and detection logic

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

  • Ability to work independently, capable of taking ownership and acting as the primary contact for fraud and financial crime-related issues when needed

  • Strong working knowledge of compliance and payment regulations, including Reg E, NACHA, AML/BSA, KYC/CIP, OFAC, FinCEN, SAR/CTR filing requirements, and related frameworks

 

Nice to Have:

  • Experience within Micro SMB/SMB business cards, payments, invoices, lending, or related financial industries

  • Experience in high-growth startups, specifically global fintechs and/or neobanks for corporate clients

  • Experience with U.S. fraud and AML risk for ACH, Card, Checks, and Wires with a global or large financial institution, and key understanding of common fraud and money laundering typologies

  • CAMS (Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist) certification or actively pursuing one

  • Experience with case management or monitoring systems (e.g., Actimize, Sardine, Alloy, Unit21)

     

Compensation:

Our people are our most valuable asset. The salary range for this role is $72,000 – $108,000 in New York City. Base salary may vary depending on relevant experience, skills, and business needs. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, healthcare benefits, and paid time off.

We’re passionate about building and sustaining an inclusive and equitable environment for all those involved with our mission, including employees, contractors, candidates, customers, and vendors. We believe every member of the Rho community enriches our ability to provide a broad range of ways to understand and engage with the market, identify problems, and drive solutions that align with our mission. We welcome all qualified applications and support each of our Rho’ers with ongoing professional growth opportunities.

jobs.title: Payment Operations Associate
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the role

We're looking for a Payment Operations Associate to support Rho's day-to-day payment processing. You'll process client repayments, issue rewards and credits, resolve payment exceptions, and keep credit and card program settings up to date, working alongside Credit Risk, Client Services, Fraud, Compliance, and our partner bank. The work is deadline-driven and detail-oriented, and it feeds directly into client statements and month-end close.

What you will do

  • Process client repayments. Run recurring ACH pulls for monthly credit repayments on a fixed due-date schedule, handling non-standard accounts manually, and process interim payments as they arise. Confirm each payment is captured accurately from initiation through posting.

  • Issue rewards, credits, and incentives. Calculate and release cashback rewards on a set monthly schedule, reconcile against system-generated figures, and process statement credits, sign-up bonuses, and promotional incentives with the appropriate review and approval. Provide cashback breakdowns to clients on request.

  • Maintain credit and card program settings. Update client credit limits, payment terms, statement cycles and custom pricing, keeping records consistent across systems and documenting every change.

  • Manage wire operations. Handle wire trace requests, recalls, returns, and non-posted wires with our partner bank, and administer enrollments and limit changes for drawdown wire services.

  • Manage ACH operations. Initiate ACH returns and reversals in line with NACHA rules, applying the correct return code and meeting NACHA return/reversal timeframes that apply to each request.

  • Support fraud and credit review. Expedite settlement on transactions once Fraud or Credit has approved them, and hold transactions for review when something looks unusual. Manage RDC returns with outreach to the relevant teams, and set the appropriate settlement delay or instant release on credit repayments based on client credit risk.

  • Report on delinquency. Produce a weekly past-due report for Credit Risk, Finance, Client Services, and Fraud, monitor 30-day credit repayment returns and overdue balances daily, and escalate for client outreach.

  • Route compliance, fraud and legal escalations. Flag sanctions-related inquiries from our partner bank to the right internal teams, forward legal notices to Legal, coordinate Letter of Indemnity and Hold Harmless requests with the Fraud team and request limit increases when transaction thresholds are reached.

  • Support our Letter of Credit program. Coordinate Standby Letters of Credit with our partner bank, fund the collateral account, process the associated fees, and provide Client Services with the figures for month-end fee statements.

  • Improve the process. Identify manual steps worth automating, keep procedure documentation current, and partner with Product and Engineering to close gaps in payment workflows.

 

You have

  • 2+ years in payment operations, banking operations, treasury operations, or a similar function at a fintech, bank, or payment processor.

  • Working knowledge of payment rails — ACH, Fedwire, RTP, card networks, and remote deposit — and what happens when a payment fails, returns, or settles late.

  • Exceptional attention to detail. You reconcile before you release, and you catch the transposed digit.

  • Comfort with recurring hard deadlines and high transaction volume without losing accuracy.

  • Hands-on with operational tooling: ticketing systems (Jira), BI dashboards (Looker), spreadsheets, and bank portals. SQL is a plus, not a requirement.

  • Clear written communicator. Much of this role is coordinating across Credit Risk, Client Services, Fraud, and Compliance in writing.

  • Sound judgment on escalation. You know which items you can resolve and which need Fraud, Credit, or Legal before you touch them.

Our people are our most valuable asset. Our target compensation range for this role is $70,000 - $100,000. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, comprehensive healthcare benefits, and paid time off.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the role

We're hiring a Growth Engineer to make Rho the #1 answer for startup and business banking, both in classic search rankings and in the answers AI engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews give. You'll then extend that position into Rho's newer product lines: incorporation, payroll, and invoicing. For your first six months this is 100% of your focus; after that, you'll take the systems and instincts you built here to the next growth problem.

This is a hands-on building role. You ship production code and page changes yourself, you don't spec them and hand them off. You'll inherit a working agentic SEO/AEO system and make it faster, more reliable, and more autonomous, from the agents that sweep and fix pages around the clock to the runbook that lets it all run without you.

You're accountable for whether Rho wins, not for pages published or dashboards built. AI citation share, rankings on priority keywords, organic signups, and funded accounts from organic are how your work gets judged.

Key responsibilities

  • Live in AEO/SEO dashboards: own AI visibility, citations, and sentiment across every tracked topic, and turn weekly deltas into shipped fixes.

  • Run the weekly operating rhythm: competitor intel refresh, a full sweep of AI-citation position by keyword with fixes shipped to existing pages, and an easy-read SEO/AEO scorecard reported every Friday.

  • Ship page changes directly to rho.co through the CMS and codebase: on-page optimization, structured data, internal linking, and new pages, with protected high-value pages routed through review.

  • Own and extend the multi-agent content pipeline (research, drafting, specialist review, compliance gate, marketing sign-off) for new articles and product-page refreshes.

  • Maintain the claims and competitor source-of-truth layer every piece of content is checked against, so nothing ships with an unverified product fact or competitor claim.

  • Monitor technical SEO and AEO health: crawlability and indexing, AI crawler access, site performance, and regressions, caught by alerts rather than by a drop in traffic.

  • Build a measurement feed that ties search and AI visibility to signups, funded accounts, and CAC by product line.

  • Lead a flood-the-zone push on incorporation: the clusters, pages, and comparisons that win that category.

  • Leave every system with monitoring, alerting, and a runbook so it can run without you.

Requirements

  • Strong generalist engineering background: comfortable owning a system from data pipeline through production changes through alerting, not just one layer of the stack.

  • Deep, current knowledge of technical SEO, plus a working point of view on how AI answer engines select and cite sources.

  • Hands on with the SEO toolchain (Ahrefs, Google Search Console, rank-tracking APIs) and AI visibility platforms like Profound; you pull numbers from the scoreboards, you don't estimate them.

  • Has built LLM or agentic content pipelines that ship to production with human and compliance review gates, not just a demo.

  • Comfortable working inside a regulated business: exact disclosures, verified claims, and compliance review as part of the shipping process.

  • Rigorous about monitoring and alerting: you'd rather find out a page slipped from a dashboard than from a quarterly review.

  • Comfortable in a fast moving, ambiguous environment, and ready to take what you built here to the next growth problem after your first six months.


Our people are our most valuable asset. The base salary for this role is $140,000-$220,000. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, healthcare benefits and paid time off.

jobs.title: People Partner
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the Role

At Rho, we believe that who we hire - and how we take care of them once they're here - is central to what we can accomplish. As our People Partner, you'll be a trusted advisor to local people managers and a steady, familiar presence for employees across the business - the person people know to bring things to, and the person managers lean on as questions and challenges come up.

This role blends local partnership with broader program ownership. Day to day, you'll be the face of the People function for managers and employees in our Nashville office. Beyond that, you'll take the lead on cross-functional and cross-geography projects - owning them end to end, from design through rollout - and collaborate with People Partners and stakeholders across our other offices to make sure our programs work well for everyone, not just one location.

You'll work closely with our Lead People Business Partner and the broader People team, and you'll be the face of the People function for managers and employees in our Nashville office. Above all, you'll be able to speak to our mission as a People team and embed that into everything you touch - this role is as much about how we show up for people as it is about what gets done.

What Your Day-to-Day Might Look Like

  • Building or improving a process - a tracker, a template, a workflow - that saves the team time down the line

  • Leading a cross-functional project from kickoff to rollout, like a new performance review cycle, an onboarding revamp, or a comp benchmarking effort

  • Owning a piece of a global People initiative, like benefits open enrollment or a policy rollout, and making sure it lands well locally

  • Pulling data together for an internal or external audit, or to spot a trend worth flagging to leadership

  • Presenting a process or policy change to managers and translating "why we're doing this" into something that actually resonates

  • Coaching a manager through a tricky performance conversation or how to engage top talent

  • Answering an employee's benefits question or walking them through an equity vesting question

  • Processing new hire paperwork (I-9s, onboarding logistics) and handling offboarding details with care

What You'll Do

  • Serve as a trusted, ongoing partner to local people managers, coaching them through the people challenges that come with running a team.

  • Support employees across the full arc of their time at Rho, from their first day through everything that follows.

  • Partner on employee relations, bringing sound judgment and discretion to sensitive situations.

  • Support audit and compliance work in partnership with both internal and external control functions.

  • Own the operational and administrative work that comes with running a People function well - precision and pride in the details matter here.

  • Spot gaps and build better ways of doing things - our business is always evolving, and you'll help scale our processes right along with it, including using AI to speed up repetitive work like documentation, tracking, and reporting.

  • Be a visible, trusted face of the People function for managers and employees in Nashville.

What You Bring

  • 3-5+ years of experience in HR or People Ops, ideally in a fast-paced or high-growth environment.

  • A natural instinct for partnership - you build trust with managers and employees quickly and keep it over time.

  • The ability to speak fluently to a People team's mission and make it tangible in day-to-day work, not just on paper.

  • Exceptional attention to detail and real pride in precise, accurate work.

  • High ownership and follow-through: you take a challenge and run it to resolution.

  • Discretion and sound judgment handling sensitive, confidential matters.

  • Strong written and verbal communication across a range of audiences and situations.

Our people are our most valuable asset. Our target compensation range for this role is $95,625 - $146,250. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, comprehensive healthcare benefits, and paid time off.

jobs.title: Head of Growth Marketing
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the role

We're hiring a Head of Growth Marketing to own how Rho wins new customers across every acquisition channel: paid search, paid social, connected TV, outbound, direct mail, lifecycle, SEO and AEO, referrals, and affiliates. You'll be the growth PM for the entire funnel, deciding what to test, proving what works, and moving budget toward it.

Growth at Rho runs as a pod with two leads. You'll lead growth marketing in partnership with our growth engineering lead: you shape what we test and why, and growth engineering builds it and makes it scale. You'll work alongside a team that ships landing pages, data pipelines, and outbound systems in days, AI routines that run every morning, and a BDR team that calls new leads within minutes.

You're accountable for new funded customers and the gross profit they bring. Cost per funded customer, payback, and experiment velocity are how your work gets judged.

Key responsibilities

  • Own Rho's growth target for new funded customers and gross profit, and break it into channel goals each owner in the pod can run with.

  • Build and run the experimentation program: a one-page brief for every idea (audience, channel, copy variants, tracking, and the scale or kill threshold), a shared tracker, and a Friday retro. Ideas ship in days.

  • Turn ideas from across the company, from the CEO to the sales floor, into experiments that marketing operations and growth engineering can stand up quickly, and own the follow-through.

  • Design holdouts and incrementality tests that show which channels create new customers, and move the next dollar based on the results.

  • Own paid strategy across Google Ads, LinkedIn, Meta, and connected TV, including agency partners, with a clear cost-per-funded-customer and payback bar for each channel.

  • Lift conversion from first click to funded account through landing page and onboarding tests with design and engineering, from comparison tables to one-click email capture.

  • Shape lifecycle and nurture so every lead gets the right message at the right moment, and approved customers fund and start using Rho.

  • Partner with Growth BDRs and account executives on lead routing, speed to lead, outbound plays, and which sources turn into customers.

  • Work with data and marketing operations on attribution, conversion tracking back to ad platforms, and the weekly scorecard the team runs on.

  • Agentify the growth loop: build and run AI agents and daily routines that pull funnel and CRO data, generate hypotheses, draft variants, and report results, so the team spends its time on judgment, not busywork.

Requirements

  • 5-7+ years in growth or performance marketing, including at least two years leading growth at a B2B, fintech, or high-velocity SaaS company. You can name the numbers you moved.

  • Revenue-oriented first: funded customers and gross profit are what get you out of bed.

  • Has run a high-volume experimentation program and kept it both fast and rigorous.

  • Hands-on experience designing incrementality tests and holdouts, and the ability to explain to a CEO what last-click reporting misses.

  • Hands on across paid search, paid social, lifecycle email, and outbound; you build a campaign yourself when that's the fastest path.

  • Comfortable in SQL and modern data and marketing tools.

  • You build with AI agents yourself (Claude Code or similar). Your first move on a repetitive task is to agentify it, not hire for it.

  • Leads through influence: you've partnered with engineering as a peer and rallied a cross-functional team around one goal. Experience managing people is a plus.

  • Comfortable working inside a regulated business: exact disclosures, verified claims, and compliance review as part of the shipping process.

  • Based in New York City and excited to work in office with the team.

Our people are our most valuable asset. The budgeted salary for this role is $200,000 - $240,000. Salary may vary depending on relevant experience, skills, and business needs. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, healthcare benefits and paid time off.

Diversity is a core value at Rho. We’re passionate about building and sustaining an inclusive and equitable environment for all those involved with our mission, including employees, contractors, candidates, customers and vendors. We believe every member of the Rho community enriches our ability to provide a broad range of ways to understand and engage with the market, identify problems, and drive solutions that align with our mission. We welcome all qualified applications and support each of our Rho’ers with ongoing professional growth opportunities.

jobs.title: Data Analyst
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the Role:

Rho’s data has two types of consumers: people and AI agents. As our data analyst, you will empower both with reliable data and meaningful insights. This is a hands-on, end-to-end role that involves everything from data pipelining to delivering recommendations. You will model new data for Rho’s latest features and product lines. You will build the semantic layer that defines how Rho measures itself and turn analyses into decisions with stakeholders across the whole business.

The increased adoption of agentic tools and the acceleration of Rho’s own product velocity result in more people consuming data, more data-backed outputs, and even more business questions to answer. More than ever, it’s imperative that a data team ensures reliable self-service data for routine reporting or inbound requests while being hands-on for deeper analysis that drives decision-making.

You’re accountable for faster and data-driven decision-making, not for the number of dashboards or reports built. This is a cross-functional role that will interface with data engineering as well as business-side stakeholders from GTM, Product, and other departments. This role is based in our New York office and reports to our Manager, Product Analytics who is also based there.

What You’ll Do

  • Drive business decision-making by working directly with stakeholders across the company to scope ambiguous questions, conduct analyses, and transform analyses into clear, actionable recommendations.

  • Proactively uncover opportunity areas as a holder of domain knowledge across verticals. Operate flexibly across verticals and function as a subject matter expert on data sources and key metrics.

  • Empower Rho’s internal data consumers. Enhance data enablement through building and maintaining models via dbt. Own the end-to-end process: onboard raw warehouse data, add relevant tests and documentation, curate end-user tables, and debug any subsequent breakages.

  • Ensure that data is accurate and useful for end-users, analysts, and AI agents by collaborating with data engineering and sharing relevant business context.

  • Uphold data integrity and governance standards by maintaining consistent metric definitions within the dbt semantic layer.

  • Own BI reporting for multiple verticals, ranging from Compliance to GTM. Build or tune any required reporting, and safely deprecate obsolete assets.

What You Bring

  • 2 to 4 years of experience as a data analyst, business analyst, analytics engineer, business intelligence engineer, or similar role

  • A growth mindset and ability to quickly learn about new business domains or product surface areas in a fast-moving environment

  • Outstanding SQL ability, and particularly comfortable with debugging complex logic

  • Track record of translating data insights into actionable recommendations for stakeholders

  • Hands-on experience building models in dbt or similar data transformation frameworks

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to adapt to audiences of varying technical backgrounds

  • You already use AI to move faster, whether it’s by automating repetitive tasks or drafting initial analyses. You are curious about what’s next.

  • Prior experience in building or maintaining dashboards in Looker, Omni, Hex, Tableau, and other business intelligence or analytical tools

Nice to Have

  • Experience working in financial services, banking, technology or a fast-paced startup

  • Experience supporting multiple verticals or departments simultaneously

  • Experience building out a dbt semantic layer and refining the warehouse as a surface area for both humans and AI agents

  • Familiarity with machine learning concepts and predictive analytics

Pay

  • Our target compensation range for this role is: $120K to $150K, with variation based on relevant experience, skills, and business needs. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, comprehensive healthcare benefits, and paid time off.

jobs.title: Associate Product Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

The Role

Our Product Managers operate like owners of their surface. The APM role is how we develop the next ones.

You join a senior PM's team and own a defined part of a banking product. You ship to real customers in your first quarter. You get real scope, a direct mentor, and honest feedback every week. The goal: in 18 months, you own a surface as a full PM.

In banking, every interaction carries trust. Money moves, cards get declined, payments settle or fail. You learn how a regulated financial product works from the inside, and you learn to build products that customers trust with their money.

What You'll Do

Own a feature area end to end. Your mentor gives you a defined part of the product. You own it from the problem to the result. Frame the problem, write the spec, ship it, and measure what changed. When the data shows a better direction, bring a recommendation, not only the data.

Build with Design and Engineering every day. Sit with your designer and engineers from the first sketch to the launch. Write specs that engineers want to read. Give clear feedback on flows and edge cases, because in banking an edge case is a customer's money. Unblock the team fast, and run launches end to end. In a regulated product, this also means that you bring Compliance and Operations in early, so they do not block the launch late.

Get close to customers. Talk to founders and finance teams every week. Read support tickets. Learn how early-stage companies think about cash, spend, and risk, and bring that knowledge back to the team.

Decide with data. Define success before you build. Pull your own data. Report clearly what worked and what did not.

Build with AI. Use frontier models to test ideas, build prototypes, analyze customer feedback, and draft specs. We expect AI to make you faster, and we expect you to find new ways to use it for our customers.

What You Get

  • A named senior PM as your mentor, and a defined scope from your first week.

  • Weekly 1:1s and structured reviews at 6 and 12 months.

  • Direct exposure to product reviews with leadership.

  • A clear path to Product Manager.

Who You Are

  • Based in NYC

  • You have 1 – 3 years of experience in product, engineering, data, consulting, banking, at a startup, or in a customer facing role. Or you started something of your own.

  • You are analytical. You are comfortable with SQL, spreadsheets, and numbers, and you check your own work.

  • You are curious about how money moves. Knowledge of ACH, card networks, KYC/KYB, or reconciliation is a plus. We teach the rest.

  • You use AI every day, and you can show us something you built with it.

  • You write clearly. You can explain a complex problem in one page.

  • You take feedback well and act on it fast.

  • You take ownership. When something is broken, you fix it or you find the person who can.

Nice to have: a technical background or coding experience, work at a bank or fintech, or startup experience.

Our people are our most valuable asset. Our target compensation range for this role is $133K - $160K. Compensation will be determined by leveling and performance throughout the interview process. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, comprehensive healthcare benefits, and paid time off.

You’ll run the channels you own end to end, and you’ll work closely with Sales, Partnerships, and Product to open new sources of demand. You’ll be judged on incorporations started and completed each month, and on how many of those founders go on to fund their Rho accounts.

  • Work with Product to improve conversion from landing page to completed incorporation
